description: Adaptable canid common throughout Sacramento. Howls and yips at dusk.
habitat: American River Parkway, suburban edges, open fields
funFact: Coyotes can hear a mouse under a foot of snow!

description: Playful, semi-aquatic mammal returning to Sacramento waterways.
funFact: River otters can hold their breath for up to 8 minutes!

description: Highly adaptable nocturnal mammal. Makes a wide range of chittering and growling sounds.
funFact: Raccoons have 5x more sensory cells in their paws than most mammals.

description: Large deer with big mule-like ears. Bucks bugle and grunt during rut season.
habitat: American River Parkway, oak woodlands, suburban edges
funFact: Mule deer can jump 8 feet high and 30 feet in a single bound!

description: Very common in open areas. Has a distinctive alarm chirp when predators approach.
funFact: They can tell the difference between predators by the type of alarm call used!

description: Secretive wildcat. Makes eerie screams, growls, and caterwauls especially in winter.
habitat: American River Parkway, oak woodlands, foothills
funFact: Bobcats are rarely seen but surprisingly common in Sacramento's greenbelts.

description: North America's largest rodent. Famous tail slap on water is a warning sound.
habitat: American River, Sacramento River, Delta waterways
funFact: Beaver dams create wetland habitat that supports dozens of other species!

description: Destructive invasive species spreading into Sacramento foothills. Makes grunts, squeals, and rooting sounds.
funFact: Feral pigs cause over $1.5 billion in US agricultural damage every year.

description: Nocturnal omnivore. Makes squealing, churring, and hissing sounds when threatened.
funFact: Skunks can accurately spray a target up to 10 feet away!

description: Non-native to California's Central Valley. Makes eerie screams, barks, and gekkering calls.
funFact: The red fox has the widest natural distribution of any wild carnivore on Earth.

description: Most common invasive rat in Sacramento. Makes high-pitched squeaks, chattering, and hissing sounds.
habitat: Sewers, buildings, dumpsters, riparian areas, farms
funFact: Norway rats arrived in North America on European ships in the 1700s and now live on every continent except Antarctica.

description: Slender, agile rat that climbs trees and nests in roofs. Makes squeaking and chattering sounds.
funFact: Roof rats were largely responsible for spreading the Black Plague across Europe via infected fleas.

description: Escaped domestic goats gone wild. Makes loud bleating calls. Causes severe damage to native vegetation.
habitat: Foothills, rangeland, oak woodlands near agricultural areas
funFact: A single feral goat can strip an entire hillside of native plants, accelerating erosion.

description: Large South American rodent invading the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta. Makes pig-like grunts and growls.
habitat: Sacramento Delta, wetlands, riverbanks, irrigation channels
funFact: Nutria can eat up to 25% of their body weight daily, destroying wetland root systems and causing bank collapse.

description: North America's only marsupial, introduced to California. Makes hissing, clicking, and growling sounds.
habitat: Suburbs, parks, riparian areas, farm edges
funFact: Opossums are immune to rattlesnake venom and eat thousands of ticks per season.

description: Unowned domestic cats gone wild. Makes yowling, hissing, and caterwauling sounds especially at night.
habitat: Suburbs, parks, farms, riparian areas — everywhere
funFact: Feral cats kill an estimated 1.3–4 billion birds and 6–22 billion mammals in the US every year.
